result: DNMT1 inhibitor treatment increases CTCF binding at thousands of methylation-sensitive sites, particularly on non-intron gene bodies. These DNMT1i-specific CTCF sites are highly methylated (80-90%) at baseline and show twofold reduction in methylation upon treatment, with half of CTCF motifs methylated at key CpG sites implicated in CTCF binding.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding, stating 'they showed that "reactivated" CTCF sites—that is, bound in the absence of 5meC—are enriched in gene bodies' and noting the paper is 'succinctly written and the data presented clearly.' The editor confirms 'increased CTCF binding sites are enriched in gene bodies.'

result: DNMT1i-specific CTCF peaks participate in chromatin looping, with 45% in K562 and 30% in HCT116 residing within loop anchors. These loops increase moderately in strength (log2FC ~0.3) upon DNMT1 inhibition, forming connections to highly looping partners associated with active regulatory marks and stripe anchors.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this as a strength, noting 'it is important to also interrogate the effect on chromatin organization (ie, looping)' and that the authors 'performed CTCF ChIPseq and HiChIP' showing these sites 'participate in many looping events.' The editor confirms these results will be 'of interest to the epigenetics field.'

result: DNMT1i-specific CTCF peaks and their highly looping partners are enriched near nuclear speckles, with DNMT1i-specific peaks showing twofold higher SON signal and highly looping peaks showing ~5-fold enrichment. The number of loops a CTCF peak engages correlates positively (Pearson R=0.2) with SON Cut&Tag signal.
evaluation: This was initially the 'most problematic aspect' but reviewers state 'this has been more diligently assessed in the revised version' and 'the authors have adequately addressed my points.' The editor confirms 'the inferred association with nuclear speckles has been supported with more solid data.' Reviewers call the 'relationship between CTCF binding in gene bodies and association with nuclear speckles an interesting result.'

result: DNMT1i-specific CTCF peaks gain ~3-fold SON Cut&Tag signal upon DNMT1i treatment, and this gain is blocked when CTCF is degraded by HaloPROTAC3, demonstrating that CTCF is necessary for speckle protein association at these sites upon DNMT1 inhibition.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly praise this approach, stating 'another strong point of the paper was combining DNMT1 inhibition with CTCF degradation.' The finding that CTCF is necessary for speckle association is accepted without challenge as part of the overall supported model.

result: A subset of genes (Cluster 2) that are upregulated upon DNMT1i treatment preferentially gain CTCF occupancy, have nearly threefold higher SON TSA-seq levels, and depend on CTCF for expression. CTCF promotes the activation of genes near speckles upon DNMT1 inhibition.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm this result, stating 'they showed a number of genes that are upregulated in the DNA hypomethylated state actually require CTCF binding, which is an important result.' The editor confirms the association with nuclear speckles indicates 'a role in increased transcription.'

result: Acute degradation of nuclear speckles (SON/SRRM2) causes significant changes in gene expression (541 downregulated, 184 upregulated), with downregulated genes enriched near speckles. However, CTCF occupancy and loop strength remain largely unchanged upon speckle degradation, demonstrating that nuclear speckles influence RNA abundance but do not maintain CTCF binding or looping.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding without challenge. The editor confirms 'these results will be of interest to the epigenetics field' and reviewers note the paper is 'clearly' presented. The directionality experiment (speckle degradation) is implicitly accepted as supporting the model that CTCF looping is robust to speckle loss.

result: CTCF partners of DNMT1i-specific peaks engage in a moderately greater number of loops (~1.3-fold increase) and are located in regions of active chromatin with enrichment for H3K9ac, H3K27ac, and accessibility. Highly looping CTCF sites have approximately twofold stronger propensity to engage in chromatin interactions and associate with stripe anchors.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these characterizations of highly looping partners without specific critique. The overall assessment that the paper is 'clearly' presented and the data 'convincingly' shows the associations indicates acceptance of these supporting findings.

result: DNMT1i-specific CTCF peaks and highly looping CTCF peaks are enriched in the A1 subcompartment of the genome, which is differentiated from A2 largely due to localization near nuclear speckles.
evaluation: This finding is part of the overall characterization of speckle-associated CTCF peaks that reviewers found adequately supported in the revised version. No specific concerns were raised about subcompartment analysis.

result: Depleting CTCF for 24 hours did not noticeably change speckle morphology, indicating the relationship between CTCF and speckles is unidirectional.
evaluation: This reciprocal experiment is accepted without challenge as part of the overall model clarifying 'the directionality of the relationship between speckles and CTCF,' which reviewers found adequately addressed.

result: DNMT1 inhibitor GSK3484862 treatment for 3 days led to minimal growth defects in K562 and HCT116 cells.
evaluation: This methodological control is accepted without comment by reviewers, indicating implicit acceptance that the treatment conditions are appropriate and do not confound the results.

result: The authors propose a model wherein DNA methylation prevents spurious CTCF occupancy and interactions with regulatory elements near nuclear speckles, with DNMT1i-specific peaks enabling transcriptional activation by interacting with regulatory elements through highly looping CTCF partner peaks. Genes near speckles may be particularly susceptible to CTCF-dependent activation.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the overall model, with the editor stating the study 'tested the impact of DNA methylation on CTCF binding' and showed association with nuclear speckles 'indicating a role in increased transcription.' The mechanistic model is implicitly supported through acceptance of the experimental findings.
